Each round has two phases: Mission Phase – players roll dice under shared constraints. Debriefing Phase – players check whether missions are completed. The first player to complete: All of their Mission cards, and One Special Mission card wins the game. Setup Mission Cards Separate and shuffle the following decks: SOLO missions VERSUS missions TEAM missions Deal: 3–5 players: 1 card of each type per player. 2 players: 2 cards of each type per player. Special Missions Shuffle the Special Mission deck. Reveal 3 cards face up. Place the remaining deck face down nearby. Gadgets Shuffle Gadget cards and place face down. Leave space for a discard pile. Dice & First Player Each player takes 5 dice of one colour. Choose a starting player. Give them the Active Agent token (Mission side up). Types of Missions Solo Missions Completed using only your own dice. Versus Missions Completed by comparing your dice with opponents’ dice. Team Missions Completed using all dice rolled by all players. Special Missions Shared Solo missions available to everyone. Each player may complete only one Special Mission during the game. Mission Phase Starting with the Active Agent, players roll dice clockwise. The Active Agent chooses: The number of dice rolled this round (minimum 2, maximum 5). The maximum number of rolls (up to 3). All players must follow these limits. Rolling Dice After each roll, players may keep any dice and re-roll the rest. Dice results remain on the table until the end of the Debriefing Phase. End of Mission Phase Once all players have rolled, flip the Active Agent token to the Debriefing side. Debriefing Phase Starting with the Active Agent, players check whether their dice complete one or more missions. If completing multiple missions in one round, they must be of different types . Completed missions are placed face up in front of the player. Special Missions When completed, replace immediately with the top card of the deck. Each player may complete only one per game. Difficult Missions If a Mission card shows the “suitcase” symbol: Draw 1 Gadget card. It may only be used from the next round onward. If You Cannot Complete a Mission If you cannot (or choose not to) complete at least one Mission card, choose one: Take a Gadget Draw 1 Gadget card. Maximum hand size is 3 Gadgets. If you would exceed 3, discard down to 3. Exchange a Mission Discard 1 Mission (or Special Mission). Draw 2 cards from the corresponding deck. Keep 1 and discard the other. Competition is stiff at the DICE MISSION agency. 
You'll have to prove that you're the best secret agent 
by being the first to complete all the missions assigned to you. Your weapons, dice and gadgets, will help you at the debriefing.
Each round is divided into two phases: the first involves rolling the dice, the second checking whether one or more missions have been completed successfully.
Missions are expected results to be achieved with your dice and those of others around the table. For example, to get three of a kind or two pairs, to be the only one to get the value 6, etc...

—description from the publisher

[Rating: 3/10] Conceptually this isn't a bad design, but it's implementation IS bad. This game just comes down to pure dice luck / rolling (usually to end the game with the yellow objectives) and there's not enough mititgation to make interesting choices after the early-game turns, where you have multiple viable objectives to shoot for.

[Rating: 3/10] A dice based game where players try to achieve their task cards (like 4 of a kind, all players not rolling a 5) each round to win. Active player will pick number of dice (2-5) and number of rerolls (up to 3). All other players will roll dice respecting the active player's decisions while try to complete their own tasks. Then, players complete tasks in turn order (task cards in hand and public tasks). If a player does not complete a task card, they can gain a gadget card (one time action card to influence dice rolls or players). First player to complete 6 task (6) and 1 public task wins. Weirdl

[Rating: 4/10] A poorly executed entry into a pretty crowded genre of dice manipulation games at this point. I suppose it is fine, but with some many truly phenomenal alternatives to this game being released recently, this one just feels extra disappointing to actually play.

[Rating: 4/10] [b]1st Play Thoughts [BGCOLOR=#FF66CC] [b] 4 [/b] [/BGCOLOR](Mar 2026):[/b] A pretty bad [i]Yahtzee[/i] style game. You roll dice, re-roll dice and try to complete contracts in your hand and contracts faceup in a public area. You can screw with each other using cards you get for sucking. I may be in the minority saying that I actually kind of like [i]Yahtzee[/i], I would much rather just play that or a modern take on it like [i]Roll 'n Bump[/i].
